page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 2 vCPUs and 2 physical cores running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the server is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core scaling is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the average category. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 420.17 GB/sec for cached reads and approximately 47.98 GB/sec for uncached reads.

The F2amds_v7 exhibits clear performance tradeoffs. While it handles single-threaded operations and text processing efficiently, it struggles with highly parallelized tasks, static web serving, and Redis SET operations, which perform in the bottom 25%. LLM inference on medium-sized models is also limited, with prompt processing falling into the bottom 10%. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe storage, this server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization, such as small-to-medium database operations, single-threaded data processing, and lightweight caching systems.
